sources.summary: NOTE: page content did not load at fetch time (no cached text); the underlying Human Rights Watch statement (26 March 2026) argues that India's amendment to the transgender rights law is a huge setback for legal recognition, replacing the 2014 self-identification standard.

BBC report (26 March 2026): India's parliament passed a bill amending the 2019 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act that removes the right to self-identify, limits recognition to biological/physical traits certified by medical boards and district authorities, and mandates certification for gender-affirming surgery; a Supreme Court-appointed panel called it contrary to the 2014 ruling. National framework applying to all states including this one.

Times of India city report (18 August 2024): a transwoman alleged a railway-police constable groped her as a 'gender check' at a Kolkata metro station; police denied it and filed a counter-FIR — shared national evidence of security forces treating trans presentation as grounds for invasive checkpoint 'verification'.
